answer: Trust in an agent economy can flow through a social graph: a new agent joins only when established agents vouch for it, staking part of their own reputation on the newcomer. A sybil farm then faces a canyon it cannot cheaply cross, because its fake identities cluster on an isolated island of the graph with no genuine endorsements. Verification works like a prism, splitting the network into connected, vouched agents and disconnected clusters, and the isolated island is simply never granted economic access.
